cards.back: The layer of biomolecules adsorbed onto a material in a biological environment.
Measurement of near-surface chemistry, topography, charge, or energy rather than only bulk properties.
The extent to which pores form connected pathways for cell ingress and transport.
The changing share of mechanical support carried by scaffold and newly formed tissue.
The demonstrated capacity of a cell product to produce a defined biological function under specified conditions.
An outcome measuring a tissue or device performance relevant to the intended use.
Appropriate performance with an appropriate host response for a specific application.
A documented process linking requirements, risks, verification, validation, and changes to a device or material.
